evidence_summary: In March 2025 the SBTi validated ING's 1.5°C-aligned emission-reduction targets for fossil fuels, power, cement, steel, automotive, aviation and commercial real estate. The validated targets cover 67% of ING's financed emissions (reference year 2021).
ING reports a combined own-operations footprint (Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 business travel) of 44 kt CO2 for 2025, and separately reports PCAF financed emissions (Scope 3 category 15).
notes: Own operations were assessed as not material in the DMA (p. 357), so the footprint sits outside the ESRS statement and Scope 1 and 2 are not shown separately. Methodology on p. 350; footprint under limited assurance (p. 346). Financed emissions on pp. 125-126.

evidence_summary: ING calculates financed emissions with the PCAF methodology for EUR 704.5 bn of lending and investments (mortgages, commercial real estate, corporate lending, bonds and equity), covering clients' Scope 1, 2 and 3.
notes: EUR 187.5 bn is out of scope (money market instruments, pre-settlement, consumer lending other than mortgages), see p. 125. Weighted PCAF data-quality scores are around 4 on a 1-5 scale (5 = least precise).

evidence_summary: ING's 2025 turnover-based Green Asset Ratio is 14% (EUR 66 bn aligned out of EUR 458 bn covered assets), driven mainly by mortgages; 87% of covered assets are taxonomy-eligible.
notes: Category depends on the proposed GAR thresholds (medium = 10-25%). The 2025 GAR uses the amended Delegated Act denominator; on the old basis 2024 was 7%, and ING says the ratio was stable like-for-like.

evidence_summary: ING treats ESG risk as a driver across credit, compliance, non-financial and business risk, governed by an ESG Risk Committee. It quantifies the risk with a physical-risk tool, a client-level transition-risk scorecard and climate stress tests, and limits it through risk appetite statements.
notes: See pp. 205-207 (risk mapping) and p. 209 (risk appetite and mitigation).

evidence_summary: ING aims to phase out financing for upstream oil and gas by 2040 and to exit utilities with more than 5% thermal-coal activity by end-2025 (one EU client remained above the threshold); exposure to coal-fired plants fell 86% since 2017.
notes: From 2026 ING no longer finances new LNG export terminals (p. 115). Not 'exit' because the oil and gas phase-out is a 2040 target, not yet in effect.

evidence_summary: ING sets annual gender targets for leadership and reports progress: women held 35% of senior positions in 2025 (2024: 32%). It discloses an unadjusted gender pay gap of 27% and an adjusted gap of 3%.

ING has policies against discrimination, harassment and violence, a whistleblower channel with human-rights categories, and reports no severe human-rights incidents in its workforce in 2025. Employees are represented through Dutch works councils and a European Works Council.
notes: Works councils on p. 90. Collective bargaining coverage, adequate wages and health and safety metrics are not reported; the DMA marks them not applicable (p. 358). That gap is why this is 'medium', not 'strong'.

evidence_summary: ING introduced a global Customer Centricity Policy in 2024 (updated in 2025) with minimum standards for product approval, clear information and complaints handling. Compensation for Dutch revolving consumer credit with variable rates was substantially completed in 2025 but continues into 2026.
notes: Revolving-credit compensation and provisions (EUR 180 m in 2021, EUR 75 m in 2022) on p. 311. Ongoing customer litigation in Spain (mortgage expenses) and Poland (CHF mortgages) on p. 310. No regulatory customer-treatment fine disclosed for 2023-2025.

evidence_summary: ING reports that it completed its multi-year KYC Enhancement Programme and in 2025 moved from building foundations to keeping controls operationally effective, under second-line oversight.
notes: The 2018 settlement with the Dutch Public Prosecution Service is outside the 2023-2025 window (p. 309). A Luxembourg AML criminal case was cleared for trial in December 2025 (p. 309); it is captured in the controversy row. Alternative reading: 'building'.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board states that all of its members were independent under the Dutch Corporate Governance Code and NYSE standards on 31 December 2025.
notes: Two-tier board: independence measured on the Supervisory Board.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board has a dedicated ESG Committee that advises on ESG strategy, integration and disclosures using an ESG dashboard. The management boards are accountable for ESG, supported by an ESG Risk Committee.
notes: SB ESG Committee also described on p. 206.

evidence_summary: In the CEO's 2025 variable-pay scorecard, environment targets weigh 10% and social targets 5% (15% in total); the CFO and CRO also have 15%.
notes: At least 50% of variable-pay metrics must be non-financial (p. 67), but most of that weight is customer, risk and strategy targets. Variable pay is capped at 20% of fixed pay.

evidence_summary: ING published its second sustainability statement prepared under ESRS, and the external auditor issued an unmodified limited-assurance conclusion on ESRS and EU Taxonomy (Article 8) compliance.
notes: Basis of preparation on p. 93: Dutch transposition of the CSRD was still pending and is expected to apply retroactively. Some datapoints are omitted under ESRS phase-in provisions (e.g. E1-9, p. 357).

evidence_summary: Several ESG-related legal matters were ongoing in 2025: Milieudefensie filed a climate lawsuit against ING in March 2025, and a Luxembourg court cleared an AML criminal case against ING Luxembourg for trial in December 2025. No new fine or settlement was disclosed for 2025.
notes: Luxembourg case and investor claims over past financial-crime shortcomings (rejected in November 2025, appealed in February 2026) on p. 309. Category set is a proposal (none / moderate / severe).
